items.name: HL · Tomorrow's order messages → Outbox
items.what: Gets tomorrow's orders, looks up each customer, builds a WhatsApp-ready message and a wa.me click-to-chat link per order, and appends them to an Outbox sheet without sending anything.
setup: Create one Google Sheet with three tabs: Orders (order_id, customer_id, items, total, delivery_date as YYYY-MM-DD), Customers (customer_id, name, phone, area) and Outbox (order_id, phone, message, wa_link). Use test data only, with phones like +2348000000001.
Create a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential called "Google Sheets" and select it in Orders, Find customer and Outbox.
Replace YOUR_SHEET_ID in all three Google Sheets nodes with your sheet's ID.
The Orders and Find customer nodes have pinned sample data. Keep it to build and test; unpin both (pin icon in the Output panel) when you want to read your real sheet.
When it works, replace the Manual Trigger with a Schedule Trigger at 18:00 and publish.
items.test: Click Execute workflow with the pinned data: Outbox gets three rows, each with a different customer (Mrs Adebayo, Mr Okafor, Iya Basira), their own order number, a formatted total such as ₦34,000, and a wa.me link. To see the missing-customer case, unpin Find customer, add an Orders row for tomorrow whose customer_id isn't in Customers, and run again: that order still reaches the Outbox with Hello Customer instead of disappearing.

walk.title: Build it: a WhatsApp-ready message for every order
walk.sample: Three orders for tomorrow · HL-0071 Mrs Adebayo ₦34,000 · HL-0072 Mr Okafor ₦4,000 · HL-0073 Iya Basira ₦21,000

steps.say: We build with a Manual Trigger, so nothing runs on its own while we work. Once it's right, we swap in a schedule at six in the evening.
Get the rows from the Orders tab where the delivery date is tomorrow. Rename the node Orders first, because expressions refer to nodes by name.
show: Google Sheets › Get Row(s) · Sheet: Orders

steps.say: Execute it once, then pin the output. From now on we build without calling Google, and we can edit the pinned data to invent test cases.
Look up each order's customer on the Customers tab. It runs once per order, and each result stays linked to its own order.
steps.data: 3 items · Mrs Adebayo, Mr Okafor, Iya Basira

steps.say: Turn on Always Output Data in its settings. Otherwise an order with an unknown customer silently disappears.
In Build message, dollar json is the customer, because that's the node just before. To reach the order, we follow the item link back with Orders dot item.
The message mixes text and expressions: the name with a fallback, the items, a total with proper commas, and a friendly delivery day.
Use dot item, not dot first. First would give every message item zero's data. Step through items zero, one and two in the preview to be sure each is different.
Fields in one Edit Fields node can't see each other, so a second node builds the one-tap link from the finished message. WhatsApp wants the number without the plus, and the text URL-encoded.
Append each message to the Outbox tab. Nothing is sent yet; Tolu reviews and taps the link.
show: Google Sheets › Append Row · Sheet: Outbox

steps.say: Now test the edge case: add a pinned order whose customer doesn't exist. Thanks to Always Output Data, it still reaches the Outbox as Hello Customer, so Tolu can fix the record.

walk.end: Execute the workflow with the pinned orders and check that each Outbox row has its own customer, order number and total.
